label: Proofreading, mismatch repair, and UV-damage repair

source_excerpts.text: DNA polymerase has exonuclease activity. If it adds the wrong base, then exonuclease will back up, remove the incorrect base from the 3′ end and add the correct base. This process is called proofreading.

After replication is complete, specialized proteins scan the new double helix for mismatched bases. Once recognized, specialized enzymes cut around the mismatch and replace it with the correct deoxyribonucleotides.

When UV light hits DNA, it causes adjacent C's and T's to form covalent bonds with each other. The new bulge in the sugar-phosphate backbone prevents genes from being copied/transcribed normally. To correct this damage, enzymes and proteins: 1. Recognize the site of damage 2. Break the sugar-phosphate backbone on either side of the problem, open the double helix and remove the bases on the damaged strand 3. Replace the excised bases with the correct deoxyribonucleotides 4. Catalyze formation of phosphodiester linkages between the next section of bases and the adjacent DNA.
Exonuclease is an enzyme that can remove a nucleotide from the end of a nucleic acid strand.

L20-p1 telomerase (candidate for a later objective)

intro_1.teaching_goal: Proofreading fixes a wrong base right away, while DNA is being copied.

intro_2.teaching_goal: Mismatch repair fixes wrong bases after copying is finished.

intro_3.teaching_goal: UV light bonds neighboring C's and T's together, which makes a bulge.

intro_4.teaching_goal: Repair enzymes cut out the damaged piece, fill in new bases, and reseal the backbone.

intro_5.teaching_goal: Proofreading fixes errors during copying, mismatch repair fixes them after, and UV damage is cut out and replaced.

timing_followup.teaching_goal: Explain when proofreading and mismatch repair each happen
key_points: Proofreading happens during copying, by DNA polymerase itself
Mismatch repair happens after replication is complete

timing_followup_2.teaching_goal: Explain when proofreading and mismatch repair each happen
timing_followup_2.approach: Draw one round of copying as a timeline, and place each fix on it: proofreading during, mismatch repair after.

uv_followup.teaching_goal: Explain what UV light does to DNA and how it is repaired
key_points: UV makes adjacent C's and T's bond covalently, causing a bulge
Repair: recognize, cut out, replace, reseal the backbone

uv_followup_2.teaching_goal: Explain what UV light does to DNA and how it is repaired
uv_followup_2.approach: Show the four repair steps as a numbered checklist that ticks off on screen: recognize, cut out, replace, reseal.

review_points: Proofreading: polymerase's exonuclease fixes a wrong base right away, from the 3′ end
Mismatch repair: after replication, proteins find and replace mismatched bases
UV damage: adjacent C's and T's bond; enzymes cut out and replace the damaged section
